title: Sender-driven gap fill; delete the chg-server pull

story.i_want_to: learn from loopctl which events of a change it is still missing
story.so_that: a gap fills from whichever machine holds the event, with no chg-server for loopctl to pull from

rationale: There is no chg-server (Mark, 2026-10-28), so Loopctl.Changes.ChgClient has nothing to call. loopctl#1014 comment 3, question 1.

acceptance_criteria.description: Every 2xx answer of POST /api/v1/change_events/:source_id, duplicates included, carries cursor: {change_id, applied_through, held: [seq...]} for the event's change, read in the same transaction that applied it.

GET /api/v1/change_events/:source_id/cursor?change_id=<id> answers the same cursor, signed over "<timestamp>.GET.<path>?<query>"; an unknown change answers applied_through: 0, held: [] (not 404, so ids cannot be probed), and every refusal is the change-events 401.

Loopctl.Changes.ChgClient, Loopctl.Changes.ReqChgClient, Loopctl.MockChgClient, the :chg_client and :chg_server_url config and the CHG_SERVER_URL row in deploy/FLY_SECRETS.md are deleted, and no code pulls events.

The gap sweep (an event held ahead of a gap for 10 minutes) and the staleness sweep (a bound change whose story is not terminal and has had no event for 6 hours) no longer pull: each raises one operator alert per change per condition (deduplicated until the condition clears) and records the change as gap or stale for the dashboard.
Epic 47's PRD §5 and US-47.3's technical notes say the pull is retired and point here; CHANGELOG.md records CHG_SERVER_URL's removal.

test_cases.name: the answer carries the cursor
expected_results: third duplicate: true with the same cursor

test_cases.name: cursor endpoint
steps: signed GET cursor for the change
signed GET cursor for an unknown change

test_cases.name: a gap alerts once and pulls nothing
filling the gap clears the flag

technical_notes: The cursor is Loopctl.Changes.Cursor; held seqs are the stored, unapplied events of the change.
The sweep worker keeps its schedule; only the pull is removed. The alert goes through the existing operator-alert path the signature-refused pull used.
Delete what is dead: no tombstone comments for the removed client.
